answer: Tuning is possible but the honest result is weak and unstable. On 29,091 inspected structures (15,693 destroyed), the case's fixed-direction equal-weight score has AUC 0.529. Best grid-searched weights (nn 0.1, density 0.3, slope 0.6, open-land 0.0) give in-sample AUC 0.602, a modest gain from fitting on the same data. Weights do not transfer between fires: tuned on Eaton (slope only) -> Palisades 0.547; tuned on Palisades -> Eaton 0.494 (chance). The pre-specified open-land direction (nearer open land = riskier) is contradicted by the data (AUC 0.379, i.e. 0.621 if reversed); I did not flip it, because that would be fitting direction to outcome. Treat the score as weakly informative, not a validated predictor; 0.60 is not a headline.
traps_or_caveats: Tuning and reporting AUC on the same data is optimistic; the 0.602 is in-sample. Random 5-fold CV (0.602) is leaky because neighbouring buildings are spatially autocorrelated, so cross-fire holdout (0.49-0.55) is the more honest figure.

Optimal weights differ between Eaton and Palisades (slope-only vs density-heavy), so a single weight set is not stable; pooled AUC also mixes fire-level differences (Palisades 60% destroyed vs Eaton 51%).

Case file fixes feature directions in advance; open_land_distance_m direction (lower is riskier) performs worse than chance (0.379). Weight tuned to 0 rather than reversing direction. Possible reason: edge/interior effects, buildings deep inside dense areas lie far from open land, and the 100 m open-land definition depends on the layer's coverage.

Uninspected (null) and Inaccessible footprints excluded, not counted as survivors (14,993 no record). 1,308 labeled footprints (mostly Palisades) dropped for missing slope/open-land values near DEM/core-mask edges; this could bias results.
Selection by outcome: layer was chosen using fire perimeters; results describe structures the fire reached, not where fire will go. Perimeter distance not used.
Wind, embers, vegetation, roof material, defensible space are not in the data and not estimated; the AUC ceiling is limited by that.

Features recomputed by my own copy of the wildfire_la.py feature logic (not the existing outputs); outputs elsewhere not read. Score My Layer not run (raster/feature-level pairing not needed; AUC computed directly).
Grid search only over non-negative weights summing to 1 at 0.1 steps; ties on percentile ranks averaged.
